mainEntity.name: How much does a Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D engine (SH-VPTR/SH-VPTS) costs £400-£1,200 supply-only, while a reconditioned unit is £1,200-£2,200 and a full rebuilt engine £2,000-£3,800 [ESTIMATED]. Fitted costs add £520-£650 labour at a specialist. Compare quotes through EnginesMarket to find the best deal for your exact year and mileage.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of injector seal failure in a Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: Symptoms include the "System Check Required" warning light, error code P06DE, poor acceleration, limp mode, and rising oil level on the dipstick . Continuing to drive with this fault can lead to engine seizure due to oil starvation caused by blocked oil pickup strainers . If you notice these symptoms, have a specialist inspect the injector seals immediately .

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt SH-VPTR engine costs around £2,000-£3,800 supply-only [ESTIMATED]. For a 2016-2018 Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D worth £8,000-£16,000, replacement is typically financially sensible - especially with a 12-month warranty. Always factor in labour (£520-£650) and the value of the car. However, if injector seal failure is caught early, a repair kit and oil pickup clean can be far cheaper .

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A specialist workshop typically completes a full SH-VPTR engine swap in 10-14 hours. With parts sourcing and delivery factored in, allow 2-4 days from quote to car back on the road. Supply & fit options through EnginesMarket streamline the process by pairing you with a specialist who has the engine in stock.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D and the 2.0/2.5 petrol engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.2 Skyactiv-D produces 150-175hp and 380-420Nm, while the 2.0 petrol produces 160-165hp and the 2.5 petrol 194hp . The diesel is significantly more economical (4.5-5.6 L/100km vs 6.0-7.2 L/100km for petrol) but has known failure issues including injector seal leaks and DPF problems . Petrol engines are considered far more reliable with fewer standard issues .

mainEntity.name: Does the Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D uses a timing chain, not a belt . This is confirmed by Mazda's factory service information. The chain does not have a routine replacement interval, but can stretch on higher-mileage examples - particularly if oil changes are neglected or fuel contamination occurs . Rattle on cold start or fault codes for cam/crank correlation are early warning signs .

mainEntity.name: What engine codes fit my Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.2 Skyactiv-D was fitted with several engine codes across CX-5 generations: SH-VPTR (175hp, KE generation), SH-VPTS (175hp, KE generation, without i-ELOOP), SH-VPUS (KF generation), and SH-Y4 (2013-2017) . Always verify your engine code on the engine block or V5C before ordering - KE and KF generation components are not directly interchangeable without adaptation .

historyTimeline.h2: Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D launched in 2012 with the first-generation KE chassis and became the UK's best-selling diesel CX-5. Powered by a 2.2-litre twin-turbo diesel with a remarkably low 14:1 compression ratio, it offered 150-175hp without AdBlue, making it a popular choice for high-mileage drivers . The engine was updated for the KF generation from 2017.

milestones.description: First-generation KE CX-5 launched with 2.2 Skyactiv-D, 150hp (110kW) and 175hp (129kW) variants, engine codes SH-VPTR and SH-VPTS
Revised injector seals introduced to address oil dilution issues; early timing chain components updated
Second-generation KF CX-5 launched; 2.2 Skyactiv-D continued with 150hp and 175hp variants, updated engine codes SH-VPUS and continued SH-VPTR
Further emissions updates; 2.2 Skyactiv-D remained available until 2024

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D (SH-VPTR) is a capable twin-turbo diesel, but it has known weak points that can drive replacement decisions: injector seal leaks causing oil dilution, timing chain stretch, DPF blockage, and EGR issues. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Injector Seal Leak & Oil Dilution - Why the Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D Fails
problems.rootCause: The 2.2 Skyactiv-D can suffer from leaking injector seals due to thermal load and combustion gas ingress . Over time, injectors can loosen, allowing combustion gases to enter the injector shaft, mix with engine oil, and form carbonaceous residue . This residue blocks the oil pickup strainer, causing oil starvation and, in worst cases, engine seizure . Mazda has issued revised injector seals for later production vehicles .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace injector seals with revised parts; clean sump and oil pickup strainer; replace oil and filter
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early before oil starvation damage

repairOptions.tier: Timing Chain & Oil Pump Drive Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, and oil pump drive chain
repairOptions.longevity: Often required alongside injector seal work on higher-mileage units

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components (revised injector seals, timing chain), 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When oil starvation has caused bearing or bottom-end damage

problems.recommendation: If your Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D displays the "System Check Required" warning with P06DE, have a specialist inspect the injector seals and oil pickup strainer immediately . Continuing to drive with this fault can lead to complete engine seizure . The revised injector seals from Mazda are a permanent fix when installed correctly .

problems.h4: DPF & EGR Issues - Why the Mazda CX-5 2.2 Skyactiv-D Suffers Emissions Problems
problems.rootCause: The 2.2 Skyactiv-D's DPF can struggle with active regeneration, particularly on vehicles used for short urban journeys . Soot builds up, triggering DPF warning lights, loss of power, and black smoke . EGR valves can also clog with soot and oil vapour .
